articles.title: How new Michigan AD Trev Alberts helped make Mel Kiper Jr. famous
articles.summary: Incoming Michigan athletic director Trev Alberts is indirectly the reason for former Colts GM Bill Tobin's famous dig at ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr.
articles.body:
If you've heard the name of incoming Michigan athletic director Trev Alberts, and are not a fan of Nebraska or Texas A&M athletics, it's probably because of the time he made NFL draft guru Mel Kiper Jr. a household name.

Okay, maybe that's a stretch ... but he is indirectly involved in one of the NFL draft's most viral moments.

Many Michigan fans are just learning about Alberts, who reportedly accepted Michigan's open AD position on Tuesday, Nov. 17. But the Cedar Falls, Iowa, native first made his name as an accomplished linebacker, first as linebacker at Nebraska from 1990-93 where he was named a Butkus Award winner in his senior season.

The Indianapolis Colts selected Alberts with the No. 5 overall pick in the 1994 NFL Draft, something that drew the ire of Kiper, who insisted on ESPN's draft coverage the Colts should have taken a quarterback at No. 2 or No. 5 overall instead of Alberts.

Colts general manager Bill Tobin was later asked about that analysis, to which he gave a memorable response.

"Who in the hell is Mel Kiper, anyway?" he asked. "Mel Kiper has no more credentials to do what he's doing than my neighbor, and my neighbor is a postman and he doesn't even have season tickets to the NFL."

Kiper was correct about the Alberts pick, with the linebacker limited by injuries and playing only three seasons in the NFL before retiring. Though Tobin may have gotten somewhat of a last laugh when his newly signed quarterback led the Colts to back-to-back playoff appearances from 1995-96.

That quarterback? Jim Harbaugh – who Michigan fans know well .

articles.title: Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence: Why a TD could've been a throwaway
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence explains how faster reads are helping him make difficult throws, including a touchdown that could have been a throwaway.
articles.body:
Trevor Lawrence isn't thinking about career milestones in the midst of a 7-2 season.

On Sunday, in the team's win over the Tennessee Titans , the sixth-year Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback surpassed 20,000 passing yards, becoming the eighth-youngest QB in NFL history to reach that mark.

He's thrown the fourth-fewest passes to reach the mark (2,853 attempts), behind Jay Schroeder (2,808), Earl Morrall (2,689) and Deshaun Watson (2,594), who leads the group.

Jaguars battle Titans in AFC South football. See photos from Nashville

Lawrence has played 86 games in the NFL since being drafted with the first overall pick in 2021.

Still, when presented with the milestone, Lawrence's answer was more akin to a long shrug than a moment of grand reflection.

"I guess you just keep playing for a while and you eventually hit a bunch of yards as you go. So, hopefully I keep playing for a long time and just keep adding to it," Lawrence said with a smile.

But the achievement gave Lawrence a chance to acknowledge the teammates and coaches who helped him get there.

"I think it just makes you think about where you've been, how far you've come, everybody that's helped you," Lawrence said.

Trevor Lawrence is seeing the field better

While Lawrence hasn't spent much time dwelling on his career accomplishments, he's noticing improvements in his ability to process defenses and make difficult throws.

Through nine games this season, Lawrence has thrown for 2,284 yards, 21 touchdowns and just five interceptions, boasting a 112.8 passer rating.

"I think I'm seeing things quickly, so I'm able to make decisions on some of these tight-window throws that you have to see and just make the decision quick," Lawrence said.

An example of Lawrence's quicker processing came against the Titans last week.

On third-and-goal at the Tennessee two-yard line, Lawrence dropped back before finding wide receiver Parker Washington in the back of the end zone for the game's first touchdown.

The throw required Lawrence to quickly work through his progression before manipulating the safety 2with his eyes and body, creating an opportunity to squeeze the ball into a tight window.

"If I don't get backside quick enough there, I'd probably just throw it away," said Lawrence.

Lawrence's processing, coupled with Washington's body control, made a difficult touchdown look almost routine.

Lawrence's improved decision-making is just one part of the equation. The Jaguars QB also believes the number of receiving options at his disposal has helped Jacksonville's offense find success.

"Everyone's a part of it. Everyone's in every play. You have a chance to get the rock, and they know that, and they play like it in every route; they're winning and getting open, and they're finding opportunities," Lawrence said.

The Jaguars targeted nine receivers Sunday, something Lawrence says is partly because the team is succeeding on first and second down, allowing them to use different personnel groupings. Avoiding third-and-longs allows Lawrence to target other players rather than three or four usual suspects.

That versatility, coupled with Lawrence's quicker processing, will face another test Sunday against a New York Giants defense capable of generating pressure up front while maintaining tight coverage in the secondary.

articles.title: NFL analyst makes wild Commanders-Bengals Week 11 prediction
articles.summary: Can the Commanders shock the Bengals in prime time again? Multiple NFL analysts think they have no chance.
articles.body:
When did the Washington Commanders last play the Cincinnati Bengals ? It was in Week 3 of the 2024 season—Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels' rookie season. The Commanders, led by a nearly perfect game from Daniels, shocked the Bengals on the road, 38-33. Daniels' late fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin was one of the top plays of that season.

On Monday, the Bengals meet the Commanders again in prime time. Cincinnati enters Monday night's game 7-2 and winners of five in a row. Quarterback Joe Burrow is playing at an MVP level, completing almost 75% of his passes, with 2,795 passing yards, 27 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's coming off a win over Pittsburgh, where he passed for 409 yards and four touchdowns.

So, it's no surprise that the Bengals opened as solid 6.5-point favorites over the Commanders.

Washington's record (3-5-1) may not show it, but the Commanders have been playing better football recently. Quarterback Jayden Daniels is quietly having an excellent bounce-back season, playing with a dislocated left elbow and dealing with numerous injuries around him.

The Commanders' defense got off to a rough start under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, but has looked like a different unit over the last few weeks. On Monday, they'll have their biggest test of the year, defending Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

While oddsmakers have the Bengals as favorites, so do NFL analysts. NFL.com analysts predicted the outcome of Monday's Week 11 game between the Commanders and Bengals. All 10 picks were in favor of Cincinnati. That's not really a surprise. However, one analyst predicted that the Bengals will defeat the Commanders 63-21.

Cincinnati is certainly capable of putting up a lot of points against Washington. 63? Don't count on it. Head coach Dan Quinn should post that graphic in the Commanders' locker room for everyone to see this week.

articles.title: Titans' Carnell Tate: 'I'm excited to be back'
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans rookie receiver Carnell Tate returned to practice Wednesday after missing two games with a shoulder injury.
articles.body:
One day after placing wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson on injured reserve, the Tennessee Titans got good news at practice on Wednesday when leading receiver and rookie Carnell Tate returned.

After breaking out and earning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month in October, the Titans prized rookie missed the past two games with a shoulder injury, which affected both his development and the offense's progression. Before the injury, Tate had pulled in 34 balls for 413 yards and a touchdown.

After practice, Tate opened up about the injury and what he's done to stay active while rehabbing over the past few weeks.

"I've just been taking it day-by-day, and putting my faith in the training staff to get me back. You don't want time off right now, during the season, but it's helped me tremendously." Tate said, "I am very excited to be back out there with my teammates, and to be involved again. I'm going to go out there and try to add as much as possible."

While Tate was limited in his return, he was upbeat and optimistic about his chances to return to the lineup in Week 11 against the Dallas Cowboys.

articles.title: Next NFL Head Coaching Changes That Must Be Made After Cowboys' Switch on Defense
articles.summary: It's getting late early for some head coaches across the NFL.
articles.body:
It's getting late early for some head coaches across the NFL.

Ten weeks into the 2026 season, no head coaches have been fired, but some have already changed their coordinators' responsibilities.

The latest is Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who removed first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker from play-calling duties, according to Garrett Podell of CBS Sports. Senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call the defense for the rest of the season, while Parker retains his coordinator title.

The change followed Dallas' loss to San Francisco last week, when the Cowboys surrendered 584 yards—the most they have allowed in a home game in franchise history.

Handing play-calling duties to Mike Pettine may not be enough to resolve the defensive problems that have persisted throughout Schottenheimer's tenure.

The change puts the focus on whether a different play-caller can produce better results—and whether Schottenheimer can show enough progress to justify another season.

For several struggling teams, a head coaching change would be the right move.

We might as well start here—because it's going to take a lot more than demoting Christian Parker for Brian Schottenheimer to save his job in Dallas.

Following the decision to make Mike Pettine the defensive play-caller, Schottenheimer conceded that the Cowboys have failed to meet expectations since he took the reins in 2025—and that things need to get better quickly.

"If we don't make the playoffs, it's a failure. The season is a failure," he said. "We play to win. We have seven games left, and we need to find a run of success."

Dallas remains in contention in a weak NFC East, but the Cowboys have done little to inspire confidence in their postseason prospects. They look just as flawed in 2026 as they did a year ago, when they finished 7-9-1 and fielded the NFL's worst scoring defense.

After 27 games as Cowboys head coach, Schottenheimer is 11-15-1, and the results have shown little improvement. Dallas can score, but its persistent defensive struggles continue to undermine the team. For a franchise with annual Super Bowl expectations, seven or eight wins a season falls well short.

Dallas moved on from Mike McCarthy after a losing season that followed three consecutive 12-5 campaigns. Schottenheimer's record deserves similar scrutiny.

There may not be a coach in this piece whose fate is sealed more than Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts.

Steichen's Colts finished near .500 in each of his first three seasons—9-8 in his first year and 8-9 in each of the next two. Entering his fourth season, he faced pressure to turn those middling results into a playoff berth.

Instead, the Colts have taken a step backward.

Even in last week's win over the Miami Dolphins (which stopped a five-game losing streak), the Colts looked bad, with quarterback Daniel Jones throwing for 108 yards and tossing two interceptions.

Speaking to reporters after the win, Steichen again emphasized the need for improvement:

"I think we need to continue to get better. There's a lot of things that happened out there Sunday. I think I take everything into account. I always go back and look at the film and make sure, like, 'On this play, was it his (Jones') fault? Was it someone else's fault?'"

Principal owner Carlie Irsay Gordon has already fired general manager Chris Ballard. The Colts have also traded wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. Indianapolis will likely be looking for a new quarterback in 2027.

Given the scale of those changes and the team's continued struggles, a fresh start at head coach should also be under consideration.

New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn also made a change at defensive play-caller. This time, the change involved relinquishing those duties himself.

Following his decision to cede play-calling duties to defensive coordinator Brian Duker, Glenn told reporters he's willing to do whatever it takes to win games.

"I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," he said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So, I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran."

Glenn has won just five of his first 27 games as the New York Jets' head coach.

In 2025, the Jets were the NFL's last team to win a game, losing seven straight to open the season and seven of eight to finish it. This season, even with competent quarterback play from Geno Smith, the results have not improved. Following last week's blowout loss to the Bills, the Jets are 2-8 and have lost five straight.

Glenn's defensive background has not translated into strong results on that side of the ball, either. The Jets rank 22nd in points allowed. They have gone well over a decade without a playoff appearance, and they are on course for a seventh consecutive season with at least 10 losses.

Glenn's success as Detroit's defensive coordinator has not carried over to his tenure as a head coach. The continued losing and lack of defensive improvement strengthen the case for the Jets to make a change.

The case for moving on from the first three coaches is strong, but Washington head coach Dan Quinn's situation is less clear-cut.

As Bryan Manning wrote for Commanders Wire, a strong finish could be enough for Quinn to secure his return next season:

"Quinn still has work to do in order to earn a fourth season on Washington's sideline. It remains to be seen what the threshold is for retaining him, but you can bet owner Josh Harris would like to see it work out for Quinn. He's beloved among his players, and everyone likes him. Whether the Commanders win the NFC East or not, if they finish strong over their final eight games, Quinn could point to that as evidence he should return."

The problem is that we have seen little to indicate that a strong finish is coming, last week's win over the first-place New York Giants notwithstanding.

Quinn led the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game in his first season, but Washington is 8-17-1 over the past season-plus. Injuries have contributed to that decline, but questionable late-game decisions and play-calls also warrant scrutiny.

That initial playoff run deserves consideration, but it should not outweigh the team's sustained struggles since.

Washington should make a fresh start with an offensive-minded head coach who can help Jayden Daniels develop.

Few expected Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh to be on the hot seat this season. After back-to-back 11-win seasons and postseason trips, the Bolts were widely viewed as a Super Bowl contender.

Instead, they sit in last place in the AFC West and were the NFL's last team to record a win, earning their first victory Monday night in Baltimore.

After the win over the Ravens, Harbaugh lauded his team's resolve.

"Thrilled, let's do it every week,'' he said. "Good to see the smiles back on the faces. You cherish them, let's do this every week. Good to see the smiles back and that was something [safety] Derwin (James) said, lot of fight in this team, and we all see it, glad it was rewarded.''

It's not the first time this year that Harbaugh has seemed out of touch with his team's struggles.

Despite quarterback Justin Herbert and the offense careening off a cliff, Harbaugh stuck by offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who is in his first season in the role.

Harbaugh left Michigan for the Chargers after winning a national championship, with the program already embroiled in an NCAA investigation into impermissible scouting. In August 2025, the NCAA found that he violated head coach responsibility and failed to cooperate with its investigation, imposing a 10-year show-cause order to follow a separate four-year order from a recruiting case. Together, the orders restrict him from all athletically related activities at NCAA member institutions through August 6, 2038.

A strong finish could be enough to bring Harbaugh back in 2027, but that doesn't mean retaining him would be the right decision.

A Super Bowl title does not guarantee lasting job security in Philadelphia, as Doug Pederson's tenure demonstrated. He led the Eagles to their first championship with a victory over the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LII, but his tenure ended after the 2020 season.

Nick Sirianni, who succeeded Pederson and led Philadelphia to its second championship in Super Bowl LIX, could face a similar outcome. Two seasons after that title, his future with the Eagles is uncertain.

Yes, injuries have rocked Philly—especially on offense—but even when that offense was at full strength, it was inconsistent. Now, the Eagles have lost seven straight after a 2-0 start, and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion (Philly's fourth in as many years) has drawn heavy criticism.

However, Sirianni told reporters he's not making any wholesale changes:

"I know we've got a bunch of guys that will continue to fight regardless of the circumstances. I reminded them last night of who they were and the things they've accomplished. But you know, we've got to go out now and go do it. Coaches and players. But I believe in those guys, and I believe that we can get it turned around."

Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie has rarely made an in-season coaching change, and Sirianni is one of just four head coaches in league history to reach the playoffs in each of his first five seasons.

But this season has gone poorly. The Eagles have also had to contend with the loss of quarterback Jalen Hurts, whose season ended because of blood clots. His absence complicates the evaluation of Sirianni, but it does not eliminate questions about the team's direction.

The Athletic has raised the possibility of coaching changes, while noting that Sirianni's record makes his future a more complicated decision. His past success deserves consideration, but it should not put him beyond scrutiny.

articles.title: NFL Gameday Guide: Patrick Mahomes is looking like himself again, Brock Purdy vs Brian Flores in Mexico City and Parker Washington's rise to stardom
articles.summary: Watch Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs face the Arizona Cardinals live on Sky Sports NFL from 5.30pm Sunday, followed by the Jacksonville Jaguars against the New York Giants and the Minnesota Vikings versus the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City
articles.body:
Should it be the former, there are many footballing disciples who may still deem Patrick Mahomes as their No 1 player in the league. That is not to discount the otherworldly football being played by Joe Burrow, or the narrative-crushing exploits of Brock Purdy or the perennial brilliance of Josh Allen. But Mahomes was that special, that good, that undeniable throughout the peak of Kansas City's dynasty years that his already-imposed legacy keeps him in the discussion.

Last Sunday there were more shades of Mahomes at his video game best as he and a reborn Chiefs offense shredded the Atlanta Falcons.

The two-time MVP and three-time Super Bowl champion delivered his first five-touchdown passing game since 2022 as he threw for 348 yards and zero interceptions in a 35-13 victory that lifted the Chiefs to 7-2 at the top of the AFC West alongside the Denver Broncos.

Mahomes has now thrown for 2,385 yards and 19 touchdowns to just four interceptions while leading an offense ranked second in yards, sixth in passing, fifth in rushing and eighth in scoring. He is also playing in his first season back since undergoing surgery on a torn ACL and LCL suffered in December last year; it is a bubbling Comeback Player of the Year storyline.

The Mahomes-led Chiefs offense was famously the league's most dangerous decapitation threat, his aggressiveness and execution downfield frightening defenses across football into retreating into high umbrella coverages designed to cut out chunk plays.

It would fizzle out in the post-Tyreek Hill years as Andy Reid and Mahomes were forced to adapt to longer, more patience-reliant drives, while also leaning heavily on Steve Spagnuolo's defense to get their understaffed attack out of trouble time and time again.

The air yards still aren't close to what they were, or where Chiefs fans would like them to be. But perhaps the most pleasing sign of Sunday's performance was the 39-yard touchdown strike to Cyrus Allen and the 43-yard heave to Andrew Armstrong while rolling to his right. Here we was throwing with conviction again, dissecting a defense downfield. The latter, in particular, was vintage, off-platform Mahomes.

For context, Mahomes recorded seven passes of 20-or-more yards for just the second time since 2022.

Both cases were also a reminder of his reality. Allen - a fifth-round rookie. Armstrong - a second-year undrafted free agent. For so long it has been a mix-and-match Chiefs offense, but Mahomes and Reid are finding ways to win.

Sure, it came against a poor Falcons defense, but Sunday was also a welcome nod to their ability to move the ball without star running back Kenneth Walker III, who was absent through injury after his lightening start to the campaign.

Instead Mahomes turned to his newest star in fifth-round rookie running back Emmett Johnson as he produced a breakout game with 22 carries for 101 yards and six catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns.

"He's here extra early, he's here late, he's not satisfied with just having one good game," said Mahomes. "I'm excited for him to continue to get more and more involved in the offense and really utilising his skill set to go along with Kenneth's as well."

Johnson brings a new two-way dimension to Reid's offense, which also looked a different proposition with trade arrival Josh Downs in the lineup.

Downs marked his debut with four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown, his separation skills evident immediately as a potential difference-maker down the stretch. Funny what Mahomes can do with a little time and a good receiver to throw to.

"It looks like Pat [Mahomes] and he have a little connection thing going there, so that's something we can build on," said Reid.

Peformances like that of Sunday can nudge Mahomes into the MVP race, not that he cares for individual honours by now. Performances like that of Sunday, with Walker still to come back into the mix, can take the Chiefs back into Super Bowl contention.

Beyond this weekend's clash with the Arizona Cardinals, Mahomes and co hit the road to face the Buffalo Bills, the Los Angeles Rams and then the Cincinnati Bengals. We are about to learn who the 2026 Chiefs really are. We are also about to see one of the best three-week stretches of football all season.

No 1 Draft pick Fernando Mendoza will make his second start for the Las Vegas Raiders this weekend after taking the reins in Sunday's defeat to the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks following Kirk Cousins' trade to the Minnesota Vikings. To make your first start against Seattle's league-best defense is just about as daunting an acid test as any young quarterback can face, and Mendoza faces a similar baptism of fire against a Denver Broncos pass rush ranked third in pressure rate this weekend.

The Heisman Trophy winner finished Sunday's defeat to the Seahawks 17 of 29 for 143 yards alongside a rushing touchdown on his opening drive, an impressive first half prompting Mike Macdonald to send more pressure his way after half-time while the Raiders offense also suffered after losing star tight end Brock Bowers to injury. His pocket management and blitz pick-up cost him in the face of free rushers resulting in sacks, and there were plays he would have wished to repeat but with more aggression to attack downfield. But again, it was Macdonald's Seahawks. The Broncos defense are currently allowing the sixth most yards per game in football; Mendoza will get his chance to move the ball.

Trevor Lawrence is playing at an MVP level for the Jacksonville Jaguars, having translated last season's long-awaited explosion into consistency among the league's leading quarterbacks in 2026. The former No 1 pick has thrown for 2,284 yards and 21 touchdowns to just five interceptions with a third-ranked passer rating of 112.8 behind only Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow. He continues to play the best football of his career with downfield aggression, tight window accuracy, off-platform playmaking and the decisiveness of a man with zero doubts over his ability to hurt every defense.

He is feasting in unison with star weapon Parker Washington, who is combining devastating route-running with airborne contested catches to become one of the most dominant receivers in football. Washington just came off a career day of seven catches for 152 yards and a touchdown against the Titans as he cruises towards a new contract and a big pay rise.

Arvell Reese is a problem, a kind of problem the New York Giants defense has been longing for in a position devoid of stardom for some years. The first-round inside linebacker has marched out as favourite to win Defensive Rookie of the Year while asserting himself as a future stalwart of this Giants team in a dominant first year. Reese leads the Giants with 81 tackles (including a league-high 53 solo), eight tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks, four pass breakups, an interception, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery.

It was wondered whether he would come into the league as an edge rusher when picked fifth overall, but it is clear Dennard Wilson is having more fun deploying him as an all-action sledgehammer from an off-ball alignment. His play diagnosis is veteran-esque, he attacks downhill with vicious speed, his ability to suffocate runners laterally is already elite and he offers the luxury to play in coverage, line up on the edge and be utilised as a blitzer. He has been a joy to watch.

It is déjà vu in the NFC South as football's worst division continues to fuel debate over a playoff format that last year allowed the Carolina Panthers to claim the fourth seed with a losing record; it could yet happen again. Between them the Panthers (4-5), Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6), New Orleans Saints (3-6) and Atlanta Falcons (3-7) hold a combined 4-17 record at home, the worst combined home record in a single campaign by any division, and surpassing the NFC South's own previous record of 10-22 in 2014, according to Opta.

It is the battle of bad teams, partially epitomised on Sunday when the division-leading Panthers beat the Saints despite posting 17 penalties for a loss of 152 yards. Tampa's efforts to put pressure on at the top could be dealt a blow after Baker Mayfield suffered an injury to his foot and ankle area in Week Nine against the Chicago Bears, putting his status to face the Lions in doubt. With that said, their best work has come on the ground this season as the only team averaging more rushing yards per game (163.9) than passing yards (141.9).

The NFL celebrates its ninth and final international game of the season on Sunday night when the San Francisco 49ers face the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, which returns to the schedule for the first time since 2022 following renovations to the Estadio Azteca. It pits two contenders against one another, Kirk Cousins' return having ignited Minnesota's limping offense and Brock Purdy soaring among the MVP contenders at the front of a San Francisco Super Bowl charge.

Minnesota arrive 7-2 after dismantling Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers in an eight-sack performance from Brian Flores' frightening defense, while the 49ers just put up 46 points in a win over the Dallas Cowboys that saw Christian McCaffrey erupt for 223 yards and three touchdowns from scrimmage. It is the Vikings and their league-leading scoring defense versus the 49ers and an offense that ranks first in total yards and second in points per game. Enjoy, Mexico.

Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson was ruled out for the season with a torn ACL suffered while celebrating a sack on Drake Maye in Detroit's win over the Patriots in Germany.

Patriots quarterback Maye could also miss the rest of the season with what is feared to be a fractured ankle suffered in the sack by Hutchinson.

Giants running back Cam Skattebo says he will stop his back-flip touchdown celebration after seeing Aidan Hutchinson's injury while celebrating

Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has a foot strain that could see him miss Sunday's game against the Lions

Cowboys senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call plays on defense for the rest of the season, taking over the duty from defensive coordinator Christian Parker

Bengals QB and MVP favourite Joe Burrow can become the first player in NFL history with at least three touchdown passes and a passer rating of 115 or higher in six straight games

Burrow is tied for first with 35 games with three-or-more touchdown passes since entering the NFL in 2020

With at least 300 passing yards against Tampa Bay, Jared Goff can tie Patrick Mahomes (53 games, currently in his 10th season) and Matt Ryan (53) for the second-most games with at least 300 passing yards by a player in his first 11 seasons in NFL history

With a win at Philadelphia, Aaron Rodgers can tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Drew Brees (181 wins) for the fourth-most wins by a starting quarterback, including the postseason, in NFL history. Only Tom Brady (286 wins) and Pro Football Hall of Famers Peyton Manning (200) and Brett Favre (199) have more

Lions star Jahmyr Gibbs can become the fourth player in NFL history with at least 1,500 scrimmage yards and 15 touchdowns in three of his first four career seasons, joining Shaun Alexander and Pro Football Hall of Famers Terrell Davis and LaDainian Tomlinson

With 69 receiving yards in Mexico City against the Vikings, McCaffrey can join Pro Football Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk as the only players in NFL history with at least 500 rushing yards and 500 receiving yards in six career seasons

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Texans still trying to stay in playoff race but need win vs. Colts
articles.summary: The Texans are 3-6 but still not out of the wild-card race.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans keep trying to drop out of the AFC wild-card race. But the contenders aren't good enough to put them to bed.

The Texans lost Sunday to the Cleveland Browns and fell to 3-6. And there's a very good chance that defeat looms large at the end of the season when tiebreakers are considered. But with other middle-of-the-road AFC teams like the Baltimore Ravens and New England Patriots having significant quarterback issues, and the Las Vegas Raiders already having traded their starting quarterback to the Minnesota Vikings, nobody seems out of contention.

The 3-7 Indianapolis Colts are one of the exceptions. One of the biggest sellers at the trade deadline travels to Houston to take on the Texans for a Thursday night matchup that looked better when the schedule was set.

The Colts started 0-2, including an overtime loss at Kansas City, then won two straight to reach 2-2. Then it started to go bad and hit its nadir with a home loss to the Tennessee Titans. That's still the Titans' only win this season. Colts general manager Chris Ballard was fired, head coach Shane Steichen is likely to be fired during the season or afterward, and the Colts traded many big-name players such as Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.

Still, playing in primetime often brings out the best effort in a losing team, as we saw with the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday. Perhaps the Colts can make it interesting. It's not like the Texans have been impressive this season.

One of the Texans' disappointing losses was at Indianapolis earlier this season, when in Week 3 the Colts got a late drive together and hit a game-winning field goal in the final seconds. Houston has gotten a big season from quarterback C.J. Stroud, but its defense, which was supposed to be one of the NFL's best, has repeatedly let the team down. In each of Houston's six losses, the opponent put together a game-winning drive in the final minutes of regulation or in overtime.

And through it all, Houston is still alive. The Texans have a 36% shot to make the playoffs, according to DVOA. First, they can't trip up against the Colts.

This is an easy one. Though both teams, somehow, have three wins each, they're in different mindsets. The Colts traded off multiple players, and while a win over the Dolphins was a nice reprieve in a lost season, they are going nowhere. The Texans still should feel some hope of getting back in the AFC wild-card race because they have talent and the teams at the bottom of the wild-card standings aren't that good. There's no incentive for the Colts to lose because the Jets own their 2027 first-round pick. But a win wouldn't do much for them either. The Texans can't afford to lose this one, though we've said that before and it hasn't mattered.

One of the weirdest stories of around the trading deadline was the Colts not trading Taylor despite some reported strong offers that included a second-round pick and more, then continuing with Taylor as a committee back with Seth McGowan. Taylor has had a slight edge in carries the past few weeks over McGowan. That made sense before the trading deadline as the Colts tried to maintain Taylor's value, but didn't make much sense last week with the deadline passed as Taylor had 16 carries to 12 for McGowan. It's odd to think that the Colts value Taylor so highly they wouldn't trade a 27-year-old back in a lost season with a long rebuild ahead, but still give McGowan so many carries. Quarterback Daniel Jones is having a miserable season (but the Colts still refuse to bench him) so the team's only real path to win is to ride the running game. We'll see how much Taylor is involved in that on Thursday night.

There may be better ways to spend your time on Thursday night, but if you're going to watch this one, here's a betting breakdown. The Texans, now 3-6 on the season and coming off blowing a 17-0 lead against the Cleveland Browns, opened as a 10-point home favorite and the line has moved out to -12.5. I spoke to a few sportsbooks this week and respected action has come in on Houston at -10, -11 and -11.5 to push the number up. As disappointing as the Texans have been, the Colts are now playing out the string in a season in which they NY Jets own their first-round pick thanks to the disastrous Sauce Gardner trade. Indianapolis had lost five in a row before an uninspiring 24-22 non-covering win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The public is backing the Texans again, but this seems like too many points. Indianapolis still has Jonathan Taylor, and hopefully a little dignity to keep this within the number. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

In a week defined by big spreads, the Texans are favored by 12.5 points as they host the Colts on Thursday. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the game.

1. Can David Montgomery get anything going? The Houston running game has been stuck in neutral all year, averaging just 3.6 YPC. Montgomery himself is at a paltry 2.7 YPC, and he's missed four weeks with a groin injury. But with six teams on bye in Week 12, some fantasy managers will have to trust Montgomery right away. Same goes for the Texans, as Woody Marks (concussion) won't play.

2. Can Jonathan Taylor survive in a struggling Indianapolis offense? The Colts haven't gone past 276 yards of offense in their last four starts, shipwrecked by injuries and the poor play of QB Daniel Jones. Indy has also traded multiple players from its offense. Taylor has to share more than usual, as rookie Seth McGowan has been a quick study.

3. Is Nico Collins back to his target-hog days? The Texans have been spreading the ball around for most of the year in the passing game, but Collins finally asserted himself last week, commanding 16 targets against Cleveland. Collins wasn't available when the teams last played, a key factor in Indy's stunning upset. — Scott Pianowski

Check out more of Scott's work at the Yahoo Sports fantasy hub .

articles.title: Baker Mayfield Gives Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Bucs QB's Status vs. Lions
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is "trending toward" playing on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, NFL insider James Palmer reported Thursday.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is "trending toward" playing on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, NFL insider James Palmer reported Thursday.

Mayfield suffered a foot sprain during Tampa Bay's 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8. He's still dealing with pain from the injury but is "pushing through it," according to Palmer.

Mayfield told reporters that he "felt good" during a press conference on Thursday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Mayfield said he practiced in a "limited fashion."

"Just trying to get as much as I can in," Mayfield said about his practice. "The mental side of it. Hopefully, [I can] get more tomorrow and go from there."

When asked if he felt like he could play this week, Mayfield nodded and confirmed: "I'm ready."

The 31-year-old signed a three-year, $165 million contract extension this offseason, but the early production has left a lot to be desired. Mayfield opened the 2026 season with three consecutive losses before dislocating his thumb during a 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3.

The thumb injury held him out of action for three games. After Mayfield returned, he led the Buccaneers to two crucial divisional victories over the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons — although the team didn't need him to complete a single pass in the latter contest.

The Buccaneers went into their Week 10 bye with a 3-6 record, but they can still win a division title in the NFC South despite their struggles. Although they currently trail the Panthers by one game, ESPN Analytics gives the Buccaneers a 61 percent chance of winning the division this season.

Mayfield has completed 60.6 percent of his passes for 922 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions in six games.
